value.body: A quantitative analyst uses mathematics, statistics and programming to build models for pricing, trading or risk in finance. Banks, trading firms, asset managers and global finance back offices in India hire them. A day involves analysing data, coding and testing models, and explaining results to traders or risk teams.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Sc / M.Sc Mathematics or Statistics, B.Tech; often a master's

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers enter through campus hiring at institutes with strong maths and engineering programmes, or as risk or data analysts before moving into quant roles. Selection often includes tests in probability, statistics and coding.

value.title: At a glance
items: Entry is competitive; many roles prefer a master's or strong competitive-exam background.
Common next roles: senior quant, quant researcher, risk modelling lead.
Model validation and risk roles are common entry points at banks.
